newsitem.title: UK: CAA to shorten flight intervals at London airports.
newsitem.headline: CAA to shorten flight intervals at London airports.

text.p: Britain's Civil Aviation Authority confirmed on Thursday it planned to reduce fair-weather landing distances between following aircraft at London's Heathrow and Gatwick airports next month.
A spokesman said reducing the minimum distance between aircraft was designed to help clear delays when aircraft were queuing up to land, and would not increase traffic capacity at the two airports.

"The normal separation is three nautical miles but to reduce delays at the airports when the weather is absolutely perfect and it is safe to do so, the separation will be reduced to 2-1/2 nautical miles," CAA spokesman Chris Mason said.
"It is not a move to increase capacity at the airports because it can only be used infrequently."

He said shortening the gap was already normal practice at airports in mainland Europe and the United States, but it only happened during daylight hours and when weather conditions were perfect, giving at least 10 kilometres of visibility and a direct headwind.
Heathrow and Gatwick are owned by BAA Plc.
